title: Lopi Parlor Wood Stove Owner's Manual (100-01141)
licence_note: Manufacturer's manual, copyright Travis Industries. Read by L8 2026-11-16 (PDF copy hosted by a parts retailer). Facts used: 'Overnight Burn' steps (high burn about 15 minutes, load as much wood as possible in large pieces, 15 more minutes on high, then air control to low; stove still hot with embers in the morning); stove thermometer for over-firing; young children supervised in the same room.

title: Wood Stove Owner's Manual, Part 1 of 2: Safety Notifications and General Information (46231_UA, 2023-04-28)
licence_note: Manufacturer's manual, copyright Stove Builder International. Read by L8 2026-11-16. Facts used: manufacturer-set minimum low burn rate must not be altered; wood must be flaming brightly before the air is reduced or the fire can smoulder; smouldering smoky fires quickly build creosote; a smaller fire giving 3 to 4 hours is preferable to a fully loaded firebox for a much longer burn; a CO detector and smoke detector are required in the room where the stove is installed.

title: Unintentional Firearm Injury Deaths Among Children and Adolescents Aged 0-17 Years: National Violent Death Reporting System, United States, 2003-2021 (MMWR 2023;72(50):1338-1345)
licence_note: US federal government work. Read by L8 2026-11-16 (MMWR PDF). Facts used: 1,262 deaths; stored loaded 73.8% and unlocked 76.2% where known; unlocked guns accessed from nightstand/bed 30.0%, shelf/closet 18.6%, vehicle 12.5%, bag/purse/clothing 8.8%; playing with or showing 66.6%; thought unloaded/safety/magazine 20.5%; mistaken for toy 10.6% (28.0% aged 0-5); 44.6% belonged to a parent of the shooter; handguns 74.0%; loading, unloading or cleaning 7.0%.

title: Gun storage practices and risk of youth suicide and unintentional firearm injuries (Grossman DC and others, JAMA 2005;293(6):707-714; PMID 15701912)
org: JAMA (American Medical Association); authors Grossman DC, Mueller BA, Riedy C and others
licence_note: Copyright American Medical Association. Abstract read by L8 2026-11-16 via PubMed. Fact used: keeping a gun locked, unloaded, ammunition locked and ammunition stored separately were each associated with a protective effect against youth suicide and unintentional firearm injury, for handguns and long guns.

title: Gun Storage for Your Lifestyle (Project ChildSafe safe storage guide)

title: Safe Storage: More Than a Steel Box and Combination Lock (holster and off-body carry safety)
org: NSSF (National Shooting Sports Foundation), Let's Go Shooting
licence_note: Copyright National Shooting Sports Foundation. Read by L8 2026-11-16 through a fetch tool (direct download blocked by the site's firewall). Facts used: a carried handgun should always be in a holster designed to protect the trigger, especially in a pocket or purse; 'off your body' does not mean 'out of mind'; people have left a firearm accessible because they forgot it was in their bag.
